_meta.purpose: FRESH-DATA VALIDITY TEST (n=50 across 11 categories). The competitive set is derived per PRODUCT CATEGORY and held constant across its members, so the business is the only variable.
_meta.PRE_REGISTERED_PREDICTION: HIGH defensibility expected (161 outlets = hard to replicate footprint)
_meta.LABEL_SOURCE: Published: 161 outlets islandwide, all 24/7 keycard access, 4,000+ gyms globally via reciprocity
sources: Published: 161 outlets islandwide, all 24/7 keycard access, 4,000+ gyms globally via reciprocity
_meta.authoring_note: FORM DATA reconstructed by the analyst from public sources. The LABEL is external and published; the form is thinner than a real submission. This is the known weakness of the test.

form.category: Fitness gym membership, recurring access to train
form.positioning_sentence: 161 gyms islandwide, every one open 24 hours with keycard access.
form.differentiator: 161 gyms islandwide, every one open 24 hours with keycard access. Your membership works in 30+ countries.
form.undercut_on: Each outlet is franchised and sets its own rate, so there is no single national price.
form.their_price_point: See the derived competitive set for the category price ladder.

tier_0_default.why: Free. Most exercise intentions resolve here.

tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: Government-run price floor every commercial gym is judged against.

tier_2_direct_set.why: Same product: a monthly membership to lift weights and take classes.

members: Fitness First - the established CBD chain
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: Each holds a clear rung: cheapest / most accessible / most established.

tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: Same goal (get fit), different delivery model.

tier_6_indirect.why: Reduces the number of training occasions.

tier_7_new_entrants.why: Derived from new openings, not asked of the owner.

derived_competitive_set._derivation_method: Derived from the PRODUCT CATEGORY (Fitness gym membership, recurring access to train), not the owner's list. Price spread in this category: wide (S$15-400/mo, 26x). Tiers follow the eight-tier frame: default/no-purchase, cheap substitute, direct set, category incumbent (the rungs of the customer's mental ladder), adjacent crossover, indirect, and new entrants derived from public opening records.
